# Ix4 Type Definition Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Define `Ix4` as Xenon's exact four-dimensional fixed-rank shape type so the static-dimension family covers rank 4 before reverse-axis and broadcast-related trait work lands.

**Architecture:** `Ix4` extends the same `#[repr(C)]` tuple-struct pattern used by `Ix1` through `Ix3`. Later reverse-axis helpers and remove-axis mappings depend on the field order remaining unchanged.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.85+, edition 2024, std

**Design Docs:** `design/02-dimension.md` §5.2 (static dimension definitions), `design/02-dimension.md` §5.10 (reverse-axis helper pattern), `design/02-dimension.md` §11 Decision 1 (supported fixed ranks)

**Prerequisites:** W2T5 must be complete.

---

### Task 1: Replace the `Ix4` scaffold with the documented type definition

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/dimension/static.rs`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the complete `static.rs` file with the exact `Ix4` definition**

Replace `src/dimension/static.rs` with the following content:

```rust
/// Zero-dimensional (scalar) dimension. ZST.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
pub struct Ix0;

/// One-dimensional dimension.
///
/// `#[repr(C)]` is required because `slice()` reinterprets `&Self` as `&[usize; 1]`
/// via pointer cast; this is only safe because `repr(C)` guarantees the `usize`
/// field is laid out at offset 0.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
pub struct Ix1(pub usize);

/// Two-dimensional dimension.
///
/// `#[repr(C)]` is required because `slice()` reinterprets `&Self` as `&[usize; 2]`
/// via pointer cast; this is only safe because `repr(C)` guarantees the `usize`
/// fields are laid out contiguously starting at offset 0.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
pub struct Ix2(pub usize, pub usize);

/// Three-dimensional dimension.
///
/// `#[repr(C)]` is required because `slice()` reinterprets `&Self` as `&[usize; 3]`
/// via pointer cast; this is only safe because `repr(C)` guarantees the `usize`
/// fields are laid out contiguously starting at offset 0.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
pub struct Ix3(pub usize, pub usize, pub usize);

/// Four-dimensional dimension.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
pub struct Ix4(pub usize, pub usize, pub usize, pub usize);

pub struct Ix5;
pub struct Ix6;
```
